_about: Maple Grove's townsfolk (Alex, 2026-11-17): people with no part in the story, there to make the town feel alive (scripts/townsfolk.gd). They wander the town, sit on its benches, drop into the Cappuccino Cafe to read, and go home at dusk. Talking to one gets a single short line, picked from 'lines' by who they are (a line's 'who' lists the tags a speaker must have; none means anyone). Some days one wants a sweater ('want_chance'): a red pin bobs over their head and Nora can sell them one with the haggle panel. 'people' are also character entries for Body.load_character (Data.character falls back to this file): 'model' is the rigged model, the anim speeds are already multiplied by 'scale', 'lid_rest' holds the upper lids partly down at rest (face.gd; at 0 the eyes stare) (the model is rigged at a grown-up's height and shrunk in the game for the children). 'max_out' caps how many are about at once, 'hours' is when the town is out (each person keeps their own hours inside it), 'exits' are where they leave town at dusk (until Bretton Oaks gives them houses: townsfolk.gd home_spot()). Names, lines and numbers are drafts until Alex approves them.

lines.text: I hope my wife forgives me... maybe I'll buy her flowers.
Why are you always walking around? Don't you have a job?
Hey, um... do I know you?
Don't look at the clock on the town hall for too long. It looks back.
I counted the benches in the square this morning. There's one more than yesterday.
My mum says never talk to people carrying knitting needles.
If anyone asks, I was at the bakery all afternoon.
The ducks know something. I'm sure of it.
I left the oven on in 1998. I keep meaning to go back.
Shh. I'm practising being invisible. Is it working?
Lovely weather. Unless you know what's coming.
You smell like sheep. That's not a complaint.
I lost a button somewhere in this town last spring. I'm still looking.

_about_want_lines: What anyone with the red pin says when Nora talks to them, instead of their usual line (townsfolk.gd want_talk(), the named villagers too): 'none' when she has no sweater of the fibre they want today on her (sweater_sale.gd wanted_fibre()), 'has' when she has one to show; {fibre} is that fibre's name, and for a named villager's request, 'request_waiting' (asked, not knitted yet) and 'request_ready' (she has it). {what} and {pay} are the request's sweater and coins. 'who' works as in 'lines'. Drafts until Alex approves them.

none.text: I was looking for a sweater made of {fibre}. Maybe come back to me when you have one?
You're the one who knits, aren't you? I've been after a {fibre} sweater all week. Bring me one and we'll talk price.
This wind goes right through me. If you've a {fibre} sweater to spare some day, I'm buying.
My old jumper's more holes than wool. Knit me a new one in {fibre} and I'll pay you properly.
Mum says I need a warm sweater, a {fibre} one. Do you make them? Come find me when you have one!

has.text: Is that a {fibre} sweater you're carrying? I've been after one all week. Let's see it.
You knit? I'm after something in {fibre}. Show me what you've got.
Oh, is that {fibre}? I'd buy it, if the price is right.

request_waiting.text: Any luck with {what}? No rush. Well, a little rush. It's getting cold.
Still hoping for {what}. I'll pay the {pay}c we said the moment you bring it.

request_ready.text: Is that {what} for me? Hand it over and the {pay}c is yours.
